title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-divide SIMD on fresh seed 9: composites form, carry B caps and divide to generation 3, some move far, but no dividing parent travelled 3 diameters before its split (max 0.69)
summary: Fresh runs of the claim world on seed 9 to t=400: labkit (rerun/seed9: 243 nucleations, 6 persistent splits at K=10 t, generation 3, merge/split 1.81; motion screen max 7.1 body lengths) and the author's screen.py + lineage.py on the same seed (swimdivide_s9.txt): 11 persistent splits, daughters both keep B, generation up to 3, but 0 of 11 parents travelled >= 3 cluster diameters since their birth or last merge (max 0.69). strip_s9.png shows A+B composites splitting into capped daughters after growth by merging. On the author's seeds the swim-then-divide event occurs 2, 0 and 1 times; on seed 9 it occurs 0 times.

observations.S: s9.png t=0 and rerun/seed9/sheet.png: uniform random particle mix over the box
observations.I: strip_s9.png: A composites with B caps persist between events
observations.D: swimdivide_s9.txt: 11 persistent splits (hold 40 frames), generation up to 3, daughters keep B (strip_s9.png t=100, 198, 208, 256)
observations.M: NOT reproduced with D: 0 of 11 dividing parents travelled >= 3 diameters between birth or last merge and division (max 0.69); labkit's motion screen finds tracks up to 7.1 body lengths, but none of them is a parent that then divides

seeds_run.result: S, I, D pass; swim-then-divide 0 events

not_checked: t=800 runs (seed 9 was run to t=400 like the author's seed 2)
verdicts.limitation: One seed to t=400; the author's own rate is 0-2 events per seed, so 0 on one seed is consistent with a rare event, not a contradiction. Merges outnumber splits (1.81), so the genealogy is reticulate.
